title: Sydney's Cockatoos Taught Each Other to Open Garbage Bins
subject: sulphur-crested cockatoo

scenes.text: Nobody taught these birds to open garbage bins.
Before 2018, only three Sydney suburbs had bin-raiding cockatoos. By 2019, forty-four did.
The trick takes three steps. Lift the lid with the beak, prop it on the head, then walk backwards until it flips open.
Residents weigh the lids down with bricks. The cockatoos knock the bricks off first.
In over ninety percent of attempts, other birds were watching. They copy what works.
Different suburbs even use different styles. That's culture, and it spread like a rumor.

description:
Nobody taught Sydney's cockatoos to open garbage bins, yet the skill spread from three suburbs to forty-four in about a year.
Scientists say the birds learn by watching each other, and different suburbs even have their own styles.
Would you bet on the bricks or the birds?
first_comment: Bricks on the lid or a new bin design: what would you try to stop a cockatoo?
